records.source: וּכְכַלּ֤וֹת שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל וְהָאֵ֗שׁ יָֽרְדָה֙ מֵֽהַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתֹּ֥אכַל הָעֹלָ֖ה וְהַזְּבָחִ֑ים וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה מָלֵ֥א אֶת־הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And as finished Solomon to pray, and the fire came down from the heavens and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and [the] glory of Yahweh filled the house.
pieces: As soon as Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and devoured the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the house was filled with the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.1: And when Solomon finished praying, the fire came down from the heavens and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled the house.

R.1: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from the sky and burned up the burnt offering and the sacrifices. The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled the temple.

decisions.choice: fire from heaven consumed the offerings: as at the first sacrifices of the tabernacle and at David's altar on this same spot
decisions.reason: When Aaron first offered the people's sacrifices, fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed them, and the people bowed down (Leviticus 9:24). When David built an altar on the threshing floor of Ornan, Yahweh answered him with fire from heaven on the altar (1 Chronicles 21:26), and that threshing floor is where Solomon built the house (2 Chronicles 3:1; 1 Chronicles 22:1). The fire shows that Yahweh accepts the house and its offerings.

decisions.choice: when Solomon finished praying: the answer to the prayer of chapter 6, told only in Chronicles
decisions.reason: At this point 1 Kings 8:54-61 tells that Solomon rose from his knees and blessed the people. Chronicles instead tells of the fire from heaven and the glory filling the house (verses 1-3), which Kings does not have. From verse 4 the two accounts run side by side again (1 Kings 8:62-66).

decisions.choice: the glory of Yahweh filled the house: his presence made visible, a second time
decisions.reason: The glory is Yahweh himself present among his people. It had already filled the house in a cloud when the ark was brought in (5:13-14). Now it fills it again in answer to Solomon's prayer that Yahweh would rise and come to his resting place (6:41).

decisions.choice: devoured (Balanced); burned up (Readable); the temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb for the fire is rendered as in Leviticus 9:24: Literal "consumed", Balanced "devoured", Readable "burned up". Readable says "temple" for Yahweh's "house", as 1 Kings does.

records.heading: Fire from heaven

records.source: וְלֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים לָב֖וֹא אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And not were able the priests to go into [the] house of Yahweh, for filled [the] glory of Yahweh [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: The priests were unable to enter the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, since the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was full of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: And the priests were not able to enter the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: The priests could not go into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled it.

decisions.choice: not able to enter, for the glory filled the house: as Moses at the tabernacle
decisions.reason: When the tabernacle was finished, Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting, because the glory of Yahweh filled it (Exodus 40:35). The same thing happened when the ark was brought into this house (5:14; 1 Kings 8:11), where the priests could not stand to minister. Here the priests cannot even go in.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD was full of the glory of the LORD (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the wording of 1 Kings 8:11, where the same sentence stands, and of Exodus 40:35.

decisions.choice: filled it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable does not name the temple a second time in the same short sentence; "it" is the temple of the first half.

records.source: וְכֹ֣ל׀בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל רֹאִים֙ בְּרֶ֣דֶת הָאֵ֔שׁ וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה עַל־הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּכְרְעוּ֩ אַפַּ֨יִם אַ֤רְצָה עַל־הָרִֽצְפָה֙ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּֽחֲו֔וּ וְהוֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And all [the] sons of Israel [were] seeing at [the] coming down of the fire and the glory of Yahweh on the house, and they bowed down [their] faces to [the] ground on the pavement, and worshiped and gave thanks to Yahweh: for good, for to forever [is] his steadfast love.
pieces: All the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} saw the fire come down and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} over the house, and they knelt with their faces to the ground on the pavement. They worshiped and gave {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever.

L.3: And all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel were watching as the fire came down and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] on the house; and they bowed [their] faces to the ground on the pavement, and they worshiped and gave thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever.

R.3: All the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} saw the fire come down and saw the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} over the temple. They knelt down on the stone pavement and bowed with their faces to the ground. They worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and thanked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good. His faithful love lasts forever.

decisions.choice: the people saw and bowed to the ground: as at the first offering in the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Leviticus 9:24 tells the same sequence: fire from Yahweh consumes the offering, all the people see it, and they fall on their faces. The temple is accepted as the tabernacle was.

decisions.choice: bowed their faces to the ground on the pavement: knelt and then lay face down on the stone floor of the courtyard
decisions.reason: The first verb means to kneel or bend down, and the second to bow low or lie face down in worship. The pavement is the paved floor of the courtyard where the people stood (compare Ezekiel 40:17-18).

decisions.choice: for he is good, for his loyal love is forever: the thanksgiving refrain of the temple
decisions.reason: This was the song of the Levite singers when the ark was brought in (5:13) and the refrain David appointed for thanksgiving (1 Chronicles 16:34, 41). It opens Psalms 106, 107, 118 and 136 and is sung again at the founding of the second temple (Ezra 3:11). The joining word "for" gives the reason for the thanks, and may also introduce the words of the refrain they sang.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith: Yahweh's loyal commitment to his people that does not give up.

decisions.choice: for he is good, for his loyal love is forever (Literal); for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever (Balanced); because he is good. His faithful love lasts forever (Readable)
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded as in 1 Chronicles 16:34 and the Psalms it quotes (Psalm 106:1; 118:1): "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced, "faithful love" at Readable, as at 5:13.

decisions.choice: knelt with their faces to the ground (Balanced); stone pavement (Readable)
decisions.reason: The two verbs of bowing are put in plain words, and Readable says what the pavement was.

records.source: וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל־הָעָ֑ם זֹבְחִ֥ים זֶ֖בַח לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And the king and all the people [were] sacrificing sacrifice before Yahweh.
pieces: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifice before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: And the king and all the people were sacrificing sacrifices before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the king and all the people: the parallel in 1 Kings 8:62 says "all Israel with him"
decisions.reason: From here to verse 10 Chronicles follows 1 Kings 8:62-66. The sentence is the same apart from the people being called "all the people" instead of "all Israel with him"; the wording of Kings is kept where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: sacrificing sacrifices: offerings that open the use of the house
decisions.reason: After the fire and the glory, the dedication goes on with sacrifices on a great scale, described in the next verse.

records.source: וַיִּזְבַּ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֮ אֶת־זֶ֣בַח הַבָּקָ֗ר עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ אֶ֔לֶף וְצֹ֕אן מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וַֽיַּחְנְכוּ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל־הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And sacrificed the king Solomon the sacrifice of the cattle, twenty and two thousand, and sheep, a hundred and twenty thousand; and dedicated [the] house of God the king and all the people.
pieces: King Solomon offered as sacrifices 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. In this way the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

L.5: And King Solomon sacrificed the sacrifice of the cattle, 22,000, and sheep, 120,000. And the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

R.5: King Solomon offered 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep as sacrifices. This is how the king and all the people dedicated God's temple.

decisions.choice: the same numbers as 1 Kings 8:63, with small differences
decisions.reason: Kings calls these "the sacrifice of the peace offerings that he sacrificed to Yahweh"; Chronicles says "the sacrifice of the cattle". Kings has "the house of Yahweh" and "all the sons of Israel"; Chronicles has "the house of God" and "all the people". The figures, 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep, are the same.

decisions.choice: dedicated: began to use the house for its purpose
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:63, the verb means to open or begin using something new, as a new house (Deuteronomy 20:5). The later Festival of Dedication, Hanukkah, takes its name from this word.

decisions.choice: 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep: a vast number of offerings
decisions.reason: Most of these were peace offerings, whose meat was eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 7:11-21), so they fed the great crowd through the days of the festival. Verse 7 explains that a second place had to be made holy to offer them all.

decisions.choice: In this way ... dedicated (Balanced); God's temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 8:63 is reused. "The house of God" is God's temple, and Readable says "temple" as elsewhere.

records.source: וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֞ים עַל־מִשְׁמְרוֹתָ֣ם עֹמְדִ֗ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם בִּכְלֵי־שִׁ֤יר יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לְהֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּֽי־לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ בְּהַלֵּ֥ל דָּוִ֖יד בְּיָדָ֑ם וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ מַחְצְרִ֣ים נֶגְדָּ֔ם וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹמְדִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And the priests at their posts [were] standing, and the Levites with [the] instruments of song of Yahweh that had made David the king to give thanks to Yahweh, for to forever [is] his steadfast love, in [the] praising of David by their hand; and the priests [were] sounding trumpets opposite them, and all Israel [was] standing.
pieces: The priests stood at their posts, and so did the Levites with the instruments for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s music that King David had made for giving thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever, whenever David offered praise through them. Opposite them the priests sounded the trumpets, and all Israel stood.

L.6: And the priests were standing at their posts, and the Levites with the instruments of music of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that King David had made to give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever, when David praised by their hand; and the priests were sounding trumpets opposite them, and all Israel was standing.

R.6: The priests stood in their places. The Levites stood with the instruments for making music to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. King David had made these instruments for giving thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love lasts forever. With them the Levites gave the praise that David had arranged. Facing them, the priests blew trumpets, while all the people of Israel stood.

decisions.choice: the priests and the Levites with David's instruments: worship as David had ordered it
decisions.reason: This verse has no parallel in Kings. David had made instruments for the Levites to praise Yahweh with (1 Chronicles 23:5) and appointed singers and players to give thanks "for his loyal love is forever" (1 Chronicles 15:16; 16:4-6, 41-42). Priests blew the trumpets (1 Chronicles 15:24; 16:6; 2 Chronicles 5:12). Chronicles shows the temple's worship beginning just as David had arranged it.

decisions.choice: their posts: their appointed places of duty
decisions.reason: The word means a place or turn of duty, what someone is charged to keep. The priests and Levites each stood where their service placed them (compare 8:14; 35:2).

decisions.choice: when David praised by their hand: the Levites carried out the praise that David had set in place
alternatives: with David's songs of praise in their hands
decisions.reason: "By their hand" means through them. David, now dead, is spoken of as praising Yahweh through the Levites who used his instruments and his songs. The phrase may also be read "with the praises of David in their hands", that is, with the psalms David gave them; either way the praise is David's, sung by the Levites.

decisions.choice: for his loyal love is forever: the refrain of verse 3
decisions.reason: As in verse 3 and 1 Chronicles 16:41.

decisions.choice: the Levites gave the praise that David had arranged (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "David praised by their hand" by saying what it means; the less common reading is in the decision above.

decisions.choice: his loyal love [is] forever (Literal); his loyal love lasts forever (Balanced); his faithful love lasts forever (Readable)
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded as in verse 3 and 1 Chronicles 16:34, 41.

records.source: וַיְקַדֵּ֣שׁ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֶת־תּ֤וֹךְ הֶֽחָצֵר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י בֵית־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־עָ֤שָׂה שָׁם֙ הָֽעֹל֔וֹת וְאֵ֖ת חֶלְבֵ֣י הַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים כִּֽי־מִזְבַּ֤ח הַנְּחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לֹ֣א יָכ֗וֹל לְהָכִ֛יל אֶת־הָעֹלָ֥ה וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַחֲלָבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And consecrated Solomon [the] middle of the court that [was] before [the] house of Yahweh, for he offered there the burnt offerings and [the] fat of the peace offerings, for [the] altar of the bronze that had made Solomon not was able to hold the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat.
pieces: Solomon made holy the central part of the courtyard before the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He offered there the burnt offerings and the fat parts of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the fat.

L.7: And Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that [was] in front of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made was not able to hold the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat.

R.7: Solomon set apart the middle of the courtyard in front of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a holy place. There he offered burnt offerings and the fat parts of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar Solomon had made was too small to hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings and fat.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 8:64, with small differences
decisions.reason: Kings begins "On that day the king consecrated"; Chronicles has "Solomon consecrated". Kings names the grain offering in both lists; Chronicles only in the second. Kings calls the altar "the bronze altar that was before Yahweh"; Chronicles "the bronze altar that Solomon had made", the altar described in 4:1.

decisions.choice: consecrated: made holy, set apart for sacrifice
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:64, the middle of the courtyard was set apart so that it could be used like an altar while the offerings went on.

decisions.choice: the fat of the peace offerings: the part burned for Yahweh
decisions.reason: The fat of a peace offering belonged to Yahweh and was burned on the altar (Leviticus 3:3-5, 16).

decisions.choice: could not hold (Balanced); was too small to hold (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 8:64 is reused; where Kings says "was too small" Chronicles says "was not able", and Balanced follows that.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אֶת־הֶ֠חָג בָּעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜יא שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ קָהָ֖ל גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֑ד מִלְּב֥וֹא חֲמָ֖ת עַד־נַ֥חַל מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And held Solomon the festival at the time the that seven days, and all Israel with him, an assembly great very, from [the] entrance of Hamath to [the] wadi of Egypt.
pieces: So at that time Solomon held the festival for seven days, and all Israel with him, an enormous assembly from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.

L.8: And Solomon held the festival at that time seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.

R.8: So Solomon and all the people of Israel celebrated the Festival of Booths at that time for seven days. A very large crowd came, from Lebo-hamath in the far north to the Wadi of Egypt in the far south.

decisions.choice: the festival: the Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: The great festival of the seventh month (5:3; 1 Kings 8:2) was the Festival of Booths, kept for seven days from the fifteenth day of the month (Leviticus 23:34-36; Deuteronomy 16:13-15).

decisions.choice: seven days, a very great assembly: the parallel 1 Kings 8:65 has "before Yahweh our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days"
decisions.reason: Kings gives the total of fourteen days in one phrase. Chronicles gives seven days for the festival here and explains the other seven in the next verse. It also adds "very" to "a great assembly" and leaves out "before Yahweh our God".

decisions.choice: from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt: from the far north to the far south
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:65, these are the northern and southern limits of the land promised to Israel (Numbers 34:5, 8). Lebo-hamath means "the entrance of Hamath", and may be the name of a town on the way to Hamath in Syria. The Wadi of Egypt is the dry stream bed at the southwest edge of Canaan.

decisions.choice: Lebo-hamath; the Festival of Booths (Readable)
decisions.reason: Every level gives the place as one name, as 1 Kings 8:65 does, and Readable adds where the two places lay. Readable names the festival that the Hebrew calls simply "the festival", as at 1 Kings 8:2.

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֛וּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֖י עֲצָ֑רֶת כִּ֣י׀חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ עָשׂוּ֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים וְהֶחָ֖ג שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they held on the day the eighth a solemn assembly, for [the] dedication of the altar they had held seven days, and the festival seven days.
pieces: On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for they had kept the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.

L.9: And on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for they had held the dedication of the altar seven days, and the festival seven days.

R.9: On the eighth day they held a special gathering for worship that closed the festival. They had celebrated the dedication of the altar for seven days, and then the festival for seven more days.

decisions.choice: seven days for the altar, seven for the festival, then the eighth day: how Chronicles counts the fourteen days of 1 Kings 8:65-66
alternatives: Kings and Chronicles count the closing days differently
decisions.reason: Chronicles makes clear what Kings sums up as "seven days and seven days". The dedication of the altar took seven days, probably the eighth to the fourteenth of the seventh month. The Festival of Booths followed from the fifteenth to the twenty-first (Leviticus 23:34). Its closing assembly fell on the eighth day of the festival, the twenty-second (Leviticus 23:36; Numbers 29:35), and the people went home the next day, the twenty-third (verse 10). 1 Kings 8:66 says the people were sent away "on the eighth day"; this probably means that the king dismissed them at the end of that closing day and they set out the next morning. The two books count the same days from different points.

decisions.choice: solemn assembly: a gathering for worship on a day when work stops, here closing the festival
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to hold back. It names the gathering on the eighth day of the Festival of Booths (Leviticus 23:36; Numbers 29:35; Nehemiah 8:18).

decisions.choice: the dedication of the altar: as at the altar of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of the offerings the leaders of the tribes brought when Moses' altar was first anointed, one day after another (Numbers 7:10-11, 84, 88).

decisions.choice: a special gathering for worship that closed the festival; then ... seven more days (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "solemn assembly" as Leviticus 23:36 does, and makes plain that the two weeks came one after the other, as the decision above explains.

records.source: וּבְי֨וֹם עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־הָעָ֖ם לְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם שְׂמֵחִים֙ וְט֣וֹבֵי לֵ֔ב עַל־הַטּוֹבָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֣יד וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And on day twenty and three of the month the seventh he sent away the people to their tents, joyful and good of heart for the good that had done Yahweh for David and for Solomon and for Israel his people.
pieces: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he let the people go home, joyful and glad at heart for the good {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

L.10: And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and good of heart for the good that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

R.10: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month Solomon let the people go. They went home happy and glad because of all the good things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for David, for Solomon, and for Israel, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 8:66, with differences
decisions.reason: Kings says "on the eighth day"; Chronicles gives the date, the twenty-third of the seventh month (see verse 9). Kings tells that the people blessed the king; Chronicles does not. Kings speaks of the good done "for David his servant and for Israel his people"; Chronicles names Solomon too, "for David and for Solomon and for Israel his people".

decisions.choice: to their tents: to their homes
decisions.reason: An old expression from the time when Israel lived in tents, as in 1 Kings 8:66.

decisions.choice: good of heart: glad, cheerful
decisions.reason: A good heart here is a happy one, as in 1 Kings 8:66 and Esther 5:9.

decisions.choice: home; Solomon (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the idiom of the tents in plain words, as 1 Kings 8:66 does, and Readable names Solomon as the one who sent the people home.

records.source: וַיְכַ֧ל שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־הַבָּ֜א עַל־לֵ֣ב שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֧וֹת בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֛ה וּבְבֵית֖וֹ הִצְלִֽיחַ׃פ
records.gloss: And finished Solomon the house of Yahweh and the house of the king; and all that came on [the] heart of Solomon to do in [the] house of Yahweh and in his house he made succeed.
pieces: So Solomon completed the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the royal palace. Everything he had set his heart on doing in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in his own palace, he carried out with success.

L.11: And Solomon finished the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of the king; and all that came into Solomon's heart to do in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in his own house, he carried out successfully.

R.11: Solomon finished building {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and the royal palace. He succeeded in doing everything he had planned for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for his own palace.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:1, told as a finished fact
decisions.reason: From here to verse 22 Chronicles follows 1 Kings 9:1-9, with verses 12b-15 added. In Kings this verse is a time clause, "when Solomon had finished building", that leads into Yahweh's appearance. Chronicles makes it a statement of its own, speaks of "all that came into Solomon's heart to do" where Kings has "all the desire of Solomon that he was pleased to do", and ends with "he carried out successfully".

decisions.choice: he carried out successfully: the success David had prayed for
decisions.reason: The verb means to prosper or bring something to a good end. David had told Solomon, "Yahweh be with you, and may you succeed and build the house of Yahweh" (1 Chronicles 22:11, 13), and Solomon "prospered" when he came to the throne (1 Chronicles 29:23). The wish is now fulfilled.

decisions.choice: the house of the king: Solomon's royal palace
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:1, this is the palace Solomon built for himself (1 Kings 7:1-12; 2 Chronicles 1:18).

decisions.choice: the royal palace; his own palace (Balanced, Readable); the LORD's temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: "House" means a temple when it is God's and a palace when it is the king's. As in 1 Kings 9:1, Balanced keeps "house" for God's house and Readable says "temple"; both say "palace" for the king's.

records.source: וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶת־תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ וּבָחַ֜רְתִּי בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לִ֖י לְבֵ֥ית זָֽבַח׃
records.gloss: And appeared Yahweh to Solomon in the night and said to him, I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen the place this for myself for [a] house of sacrifice.
pieces: Then during the night {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon. He said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} as a house of sacrifice.

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon in the night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} as a house of sacrifice.

R.12: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon one night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer. I have chosen this place for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to be a temple where people offer sacrifices.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:2-3a, with differences
decisions.reason: Kings says that Yahweh appeared to Solomon "a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon", and that he had heard "your prayer and your plea for favor that you made before me". Chronicles says that he appeared "in the night", as he had at Gibeon (1:7), and adds "and I have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice". Verses 12b-15 are found only in Chronicles.

decisions.choice: I have chosen this place: the place Deuteronomy promised Yahweh would choose
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks again and again of "the place that Yahweh your God will choose", where Israel was to bring its sacrifices (Deuteronomy 12:5-6, 11, 14). Solomon's prayer had asked Yahweh to hear prayers made toward "this place" (6:20-21); Yahweh now names it as his chosen place.

decisions.choice: a house of sacrifice: the place where the offerings that bring Israel near to Yahweh are made
decisions.reason: Solomon's prayer spoke of the house as the place toward which Israel would pray (6:20-40). Yahweh's answer names it as the place of sacrifice, the center of Israel's worship (compare 2:3). The two belong together: prayer at this house is joined to the offerings made there.

decisions.choice: the speech opens here and runs to verse 22
decisions.reason: Yahweh's words begin with "I have heard" and continue without a break to the end of the chapter.

decisions.choice: a temple where people offer sacrifices (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "a house of sacrifice" is.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} appears to Solomon again

records.source: הֵ֣ן אֶֽעֱצֹ֤ר הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה מָטָ֔ר וְהֵן־אֲצַוֶּ֥ה עַל־חָגָ֖ב לֶאֱכ֣וֹל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְאִם־אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח דֶּ֖בֶר בְּעַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: If I shut up the heavens and not there is rain, and if I command on [the] locust to devour the land, and if I send pestilence among my people,
pieces: When I shut up the sky so that no rain falls, or command locusts to eat up the land, or send a plague among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people,

L.13: If I shut up the heavens and there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people,

R.13: Suppose I close up the sky so that no rain falls. Or suppose I order locusts to eat up the crops of the land, or I send a deadly disease among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

decisions.choice: if ... if ... if: the cases in which the promise of verse 14 applies
decisions.reason: The first two "if" words are a form often meaning "look", but here, as sometimes elsewhere (Jeremiah 3:1; Leviticus 25:20), it introduces a condition and stands parallel with the ordinary "if" that follows. The three cases set the scene; verse 14 gives what the people must do and what Yahweh will then do.

decisions.choice: drought, locusts and pestilence: the troubles Solomon named in his prayer
decisions.reason: Solomon had asked Yahweh to hear and forgive when the heavens were shut up and there was no rain, and when there was famine, plague, blight or locusts (6:26-31). The covenant warnings named the same disasters as the results of Israel's unfaithfulness (Deuteronomy 11:17; 28:21-24, 38, 42). Yahweh's answer takes up Solomon's own words.

decisions.choice: I shut up, I command, I send: Yahweh himself sends the trouble
decisions.reason: Each disaster is something Yahweh does. They are not chance misfortunes but discipline, meant to turn his people back to him, as the next verse shows.

decisions.choice: pestilence: a deadly epidemic
decisions.reason: The word names a disease that spreads among people and kills many, often listed with sword and famine (Jeremiah 14:12; 2 Samuel 24:13).

decisions.choice: the sky; a plague (Balanced); a deadly disease (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The heavens" here are the sky that gives rain, so Balanced and Readable say "sky". Readable states the three cases as their own sentences, and adds "the crops" because the locusts eat what grows on the land.

records.source: וְיִכָּנְע֨וּ עַמִּ֜י אֲשֶׁ֧ר נִֽקְרָא־שְׁמִ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וְיִֽתְפַּֽלְלוּ֙ וִֽיבַקְשׁ֣וּ פָנַ֔י וְיָשֻׁ֖בוּ מִדַּרְכֵיהֶ֣ם הָרָעִ֑ים וַאֲנִי֙ אֶשְׁמַ֣ע מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְאֶסְלַח֙ לְחַטָּאתָ֔ם וְאֶרְפָּ֖א אֶת־אַרְצָֽם׃
records.gloss: and humble themselves my people who is called my name over them, and they pray and seek my face and turn from their ways the evil, and I will hear from the heavens and forgive their sin and heal their land.
pieces: and if {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who bear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name humble themselves and pray, seek {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face and turn back from their evil ways, then I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will hear from heaven. I will forgive their sin and heal their land.

L.14: and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people over whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is called humble themselves, and pray, and seek {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face, and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from the heavens, and I will forgive their sin and heal their land.

R.14: Then if {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and carry {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, become humble and pray, if they look for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and turn away from their evil ways, I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will hear them from heaven. I will forgive their sin and heal their land.

decisions.choice: my people over whom my name is called: the people who belong to Yahweh
decisions.reason: To call a name over something is to claim it as one's own (Deuteronomy 28:10; 2 Samuel 12:28; Jeremiah 14:9). Israel bears Yahweh's name because it is his people, as the house bears his name because it is his house (6:33).

decisions.choice: humble themselves, pray, seek my face, turn: four sides of one return to Yahweh
decisions.reason: To humble oneself is to give up pride and submit to Yahweh; Chronicles uses the word for kings and people who turn back to him (12:6-7, 12; 30:11; 32:26; 33:12, 19, 23; 34:27). To seek his face is to seek his presence and favor (1 Chronicles 16:11; Psalm 27:8). To turn from evil ways is to change one's conduct, not only to feel sorry.

decisions.choice: the promise first speaks of Israel, the temple and the land of Israel
decisions.reason: In its setting the promise is Yahweh's answer to Solomon at the dedication of the temple. "My people" are Israel, "their land" is the land Yahweh gave them (verse 20), and healing it means ending the drought, locusts and plague of verse 13. It answers Solomon's prayer that Yahweh would hear from heaven, forgive and send rain (6:26-27), and the rest of Chronicles shows it at work: when kings and people humble themselves, Yahweh hears and restores (12:6-7; 30:18-20; 33:12-13). Readers who apply it to other peoples and lands extend it beyond its first setting, by way of the wider truth it shows: that God hears and forgives those who humble themselves and turn back to him.

decisions.choice: then I will hear from heaven: the emphatic "I" of Yahweh's answer
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is written out, which stresses that Yahweh himself will answer. "Hear from heaven" takes up the refrain of Solomon's prayer (6:21, 23, 25, 27, 30, 33, 35, 39).

decisions.choice: heal their land: restore it to health
decisions.reason: The verb is used of making whole what is sick or broken. Here it is the land, struck by the disasters of verse 13, that Yahweh makes fruitful again; elsewhere in Chronicles he heals the people (30:20).

decisions.choice: over whom my name is called (Literal); who bear my name (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced says it as a people bearing the name of the one they belong to.

decisions.choice: the people who belong to me and carry my name; look for me; hear them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name picture and says "look for me" for "seek my face". It supplies "them" after "hear" to make clear that Yahweh hears their prayer.

decisions.choice: I myself (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the written-out pronoun with "myself"; Literal keeps the plain "I".

records.source: עַתָּ֗ה עֵינַי֙ יִהְי֣וּ פְתֻח֔וֹת וְאָזְנַ֖י קַשֻּׁב֑וֹת לִתְפִלַּ֖ת הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to [the] prayer of the place this.
pieces: Now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes will be open, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears will attend to the prayer made in this place.

L.15: Now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes will be open and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears attentive to the prayer of this place.

R.15: From now on I will watch over this place, and I will listen closely to the prayers made here.

decisions.choice: my eyes open and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place: the answer to 6:40
decisions.reason: Solomon ended his prayer, "Now, my God, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place" (6:40; compare 6:20). Yahweh answers in the same words.

decisions.choice: the prayer of this place: prayer made at the temple or toward it
decisions.reason: The prayers in view are those offered in the house and those made toward it from far away (6:20-21, 34, 38).

decisions.choice: the prayer made in this place; my ears will attend (Balanced); I will watch over this place, and I will listen closely to the prayers made here (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out "the prayer of this place". Readable puts the pictures of open eyes and attentive ears in plain words.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה בָּחַ֤רְתִּי וְהִקְדַּ֨שְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה לִהְיוֹת־שְׁמִ֥י שָׁ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם וְהָי֨וּ עֵינַ֧י וְלִבִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And now I have chosen and consecrated the house this for being my name there until forever, and will be my eyes and my heart there all the days.
pieces: Now I have chosen this house and set it apart as holy, so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name may stay there forever. My eyes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart will always be there.

L.16: And now I have chosen and consecrated this house, so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name may be there forever; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart will be there all the days.

R.16: Now I have chosen this temple and made it a holy place, so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will be there forever. I will always watch over it and care for it.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:3b, with differences
decisions.reason: Kings has "I have consecrated this house that you have built, to put my name there forever". Chronicles begins "and now", adds "I have chosen", leaves out "that you have built", and says "so that my name may be there". The rest is the same.

decisions.choice: that my name may be there: the house where Yahweh is known and called on
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:3, the "name" stands for Yahweh himself as he makes himself known (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11). He is not confined to the house (6:18), but this is where his name is honored.

decisions.choice: my eyes and my heart will be there all the days: Yahweh's constant attention and care
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:3: eyes stand for watching over something, the heart for concern and will, and "all the days" means always.

decisions.choice: wording of 1 Kings 9:3 reused
decisions.reason: Each level repeats its wording from 1 Kings 9:3 where the Hebrew is the same: "set it apart as holy" (Balanced), "made it a holy place" and "watch over it and care for it" (Readable).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם־תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנַ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלַךְ֙ דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔יךָ וְלַעֲשׂ֕וֹת כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ וְחֻקַּ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י תִּשְׁמֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And you, if you will walk before me as walked David your father, and to do according to all that I have commanded you; and my statutes and my judgments you will keep,
pieces: As for you, if you live before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as your father David did, doing everything I have commanded you and keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings,

L.17: And you, if you walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as David your father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments,

R.17: Now you must live faithfully before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as your father David did. Do everything I have commanded you, and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:4 without "in integrity of heart and in uprightness"
decisions.reason: Kings describes how David walked: "in integrity of heart and in uprightness". Chronicles leaves the phrase out and joins the next words with "and": walk as David did, and do all that I have commanded.

decisions.choice: walk before me: live one's whole life in Yahweh's sight and service
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:4 (compare Genesis 17:1; 2 Chronicles 6:16).

decisions.choice: if ...: the condition on which the promise of verse 18 depends
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:4-5, the promise to Solomon's line depends on his obedience (6:16).

decisions.choice: statutes and rulings (Balanced); laws and rules (Readable); you must ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 9:4 is reused. Readable states the conditions as plain sentences and gives the "if" at the start of verse 18.

records.source: וַהֲקִ֣ימוֹתִ֔י אֵ֖ת כִּסֵּ֣א מַלְכוּתֶ֑ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֗תִּי לְדָוִ֤יד אָבִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: then I will establish [the] throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, Not will be cut off for you a man ruling in Israel.
pieces: then I will make the throne of your kingdom secure, as I promised in my covenant with your father David when I said, 'There will always be a man of your line ruling in Israel.'

L.18: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, 'A man ruling in Israel will not be cut off for you.'

R.18: If you do, I will make your kingdom secure, as I promised your father David in my covenant with him. I told him, 'One of your family will always rule in Israel.'

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:5, with differences
decisions.reason: Kings reads "the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke concerning David your father ... a man will not be cut off for you from on the throne of Israel". Chronicles leaves out "over Israel forever", says "as I covenanted with David" instead of "as I spoke", and ends "a man ruling in Israel". The last phrase is the same as in Micah 5:1, which promises one from Bethlehem "to be ruler in Israel".

decisions.choice: I covenanted: I made a covenant
decisions.reason: The verb means "cut", used for making a covenant; here it stands alone with that sense. Yahweh's promise to David is called a covenant elsewhere too (13:5; 21:7; Psalm 89:4).

decisions.choice: a man will not be cut off for you: your line will never lack a ruler
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:5, "cut off" means removed or brought to an end; the promise is that David's family will never be without a king.

decisions.choice: make the throne of your kingdom secure (Balanced); make your kingdom secure (Readable); in my covenant
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 9:5 is reused where the Hebrew is the same; Balanced and Readable add "in my covenant" for the verb of covenant-making.

records.source: וְאִם־תְּשׁוּב֣וּן אַתֶּ֔ם וַעֲזַבְתֶּם֙ חֻקּוֹתַ֣י וּמִצְוֺתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And if turn away you, and forsake my statutes and my commandments which I have set before you, and you go and serve gods other and bow down to them,
pieces: But if all of you turn away and abandon {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments that I have set before you, and instead go off to serve other gods and bow down to them,

L.19: But if you turn away, you [all], and forsake {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

R.19: But suppose all of you turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Suppose you abandon the laws and commands I have given you, and you go and serve other gods and worship them.

decisions.choice: if you turn away, you: the address widens from Solomon to all the people
decisions.reason: The verbs and the pronoun "you" are now plural, and the pronoun is written out for emphasis. Verses 17-18 spoke to Solomon alone; the warning now covers Solomon, the kings after him and all Israel.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:6, with differences
decisions.reason: Kings has "if you indeed turn back, you or your sons, from following me, and do not keep my commandments, my statutes". Chronicles has "if you turn away and forsake my statutes and my commandments". "Forsake" is a word Chronicles often uses for turning from Yahweh (12:1, 5; 15:2; 24:20).

decisions.choice: serve other gods and bow down to them: breaking the first demand of the covenant
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:6, worshiping other gods breaks the first two commandments (Exodus 20:3-5) and is the sin that Deuteronomy says would bring exile (Deuteronomy 29:25-27).

decisions.choice: you [all] (Literal); all of you (Balanced, Readable); from me (Readable)
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural, so each level marks it. Readable adds "from me", which the turning away implies, and otherwise reuses its wording from 1 Kings 9:6.

records.source: וּנְתַשְׁתִּ֗ים מֵעַ֤ל אַדְמָתִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדַּ֣שְׁתִּי לִשְׁמִ֔י אַשְׁלִ֖יךְ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑י וְאֶתְּנֶ֛נּוּ לְמָשָׁ֥ל וְלִשְׁנִינָ֖ה בְּכָל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: then I will pluck them up from on my land which I have given to them, and the house this which I have consecrated for my name I will cast from on my face, and I will make it for a proverb and for a taunt among all the peoples.
pieces: then I will uproot them from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land that I have given them, and I will cast this house that I have made holy for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight. I will make it a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.

L.20: then I will uproot them from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land that I have given them; and this house that I have consecrated for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name I will cast away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence, and I will make it a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.

R.20: Then I will pull the people up by the roots from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land that I gave them. I will reject this temple that I made holy for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face away from it. People of every nation will tell of what happened to it as a warning, and they will make fun of it.

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:7, with differences
decisions.reason: Kings has "I will cut off Israel from the face of the ground"; Chronicles has "I will uproot them from my land", the picture of Deuteronomy 29:27. Kings says Yahweh will "send away" the house; Chronicles "cast" it. In Kings it is Israel that becomes a proverb and a byword; in Chronicles it is the house.

decisions.choice: my land: the land belongs to Yahweh
decisions.reason: Israel lives on the land as Yahweh's gift and holds it from him (Leviticus 25:23). Being uprooted from it is the exile the covenant warned of (Deuteronomy 28:63-64), which Chronicles tells at its end (36:17-20).

decisions.choice: a proverb and a byword: a saying about the house's fate and a sharp taunt
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:7: the first word is a saying people quote, the second a word of mockery. The same pair appears in the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:37).

decisions.choice: pull the people up by the roots; reject ... turn my face away from it; tell of what happened to it as a warning, and make fun of it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names "them" as the people and reuses its wording from 1 Kings 9:7, which explains the two nouns and "cast from my face".

records.source: וְהַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה עֶלְי֔וֹן לְכָל־עֹבֵ֥ר עָלָ֖יו יִשֹּׁ֑ם וְאָמַ֗ר בַּמֶּ֨ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כָּ֔כָה לָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְלַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And the house this which was exalted, every [one] passing by it will be appalled and will say, For what did Yahweh do thus to the land this and to the house this?
pieces: And this house, high as it once stood, will leave everyone who passes by it appalled. They will ask, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dealt like this with this land and this house?'

L.21: And [as for] this house, which was exalted, everyone passing by it will be appalled and will say, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done thus to this land and to this house?'

R.21: This temple was once high and grand, but everyone who passes by it will be shocked. They will ask, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done this to the land and to this temple?'

decisions.choice: which was exalted: read as "lofty as it was"
alternatives: will become a heap of ruins
decisions.reason: Chronicles has "which was exalted" where 1 Kings 9:8 has "will be high". Both are hard to fit with the ruin the verse describes, and are best taken as a contrast: the house that was so lofty will leave all who pass appalled. Some early translations read "will become a heap of ruins", which may reflect a different Hebrew word (compare Micah 3:12).

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:8 without "and will hiss"; the question of Deuteronomy 29
decisions.reason: Kings says the passer-by "will be appalled and will hiss"; Chronicles has only "will be appalled". Deuteronomy foresees the nations asking the same question about the ruined land (Deuteronomy 29:23-25; compare Jeremiah 22:8-9).

decisions.choice: appalled: struck with horror at a ruin
decisions.reason: The verb means to be devastated or stunned, the reaction to a place laid waste (Jeremiah 19:8; 49:17).

decisions.choice: high as it once stood (Balanced); was once high and grand, but (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the contrast explicit, as at 1 Kings 9:8, and use "once" for the past tense of Chronicles.

records.source: וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָֽזְב֜וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹצִיאָם֮ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיַּחֲזִ֨יקוּ֙ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם וַיַּֽעַבְד֑וּם עַל־כֵּן֙ הֵבִ֣יא עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃פ
records.gloss: And they will say, Because that they forsook Yahweh [the] God of their fathers who brought them out from [the] land of Egypt, and they took hold of gods other and bowed down to them and served them; therefore he has brought on them all the disaster this.
pieces: And people will answer, 'Because they abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they embraced other gods and worshiped and served them. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought all this disaster on them.'"

L.22: And they will say, 'Because they forsook {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them; therefore {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought on them all this disaster.'"

R.22: And people will answer, 'It is because they left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of Egypt. They held on to other gods and worshiped and served them. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought all this trouble on them.'"

decisions.choice: the parallel 1 Kings 9:9, with differences
decisions.reason: Kings has "Yahweh their God, who brought their fathers out" and "therefore Yahweh has brought". Chronicles has "Yahweh the God of their fathers, who brought them out", a title it often uses (for example 13:12, 18; 15:12), and "therefore he has brought", without the name.

decisions.choice: took hold of: clung to, attached themselves firmly to
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:9: Israel let go of Yahweh and held fast to other gods instead.

decisions.choice: disaster: calamity, harm that comes on them
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:9, the word means the ruin Yahweh brings as judgment, not moral wrong.

decisions.choice: ancestors; people will answer
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:9, Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers" and name the speakers as "people". The closing double quote ends Yahweh's speech that began in verse 12.
